MAPBERN: meta-analytic predictive prior and mixture likelihood

Source: vignettes/mapbern.Rmd
mapbern.Rmd
library(bssd)

Model

Brock et al. (2023) estimate the posterior probability that the event probability per unit time on study drug, \(\pi_d\), exceeds that on control, \(\pi_c\), in an ongoing blinded study. Each subject with time at risk \(t_i\) has the event with probability \(1 - (1 - \pi)^{t_i}\) on the arm received, and the likelihood of the blinded data is the mixture over the two arms weighted by the randomization probabilities. The prior of \(\pi_c\) is the meta-analytic predictive (MAP) prior from historical control arms, \[ \pi_j \mid a, b \sim \mathrm{Beta}(a b N, (1 - a) b N), \quad a \sim \mathrm{Beta}(1/3, 1/3), \quad b \sim \mathrm{Beta}(5, 5), \] where \(N\) is the total number of historical subjects, \(a\) is the mean event probability and \(b\) discounts the historical information. The prior of \(\pi_d\) is Beta(1/3, 1/3).

map_beta() integrates the posterior of \((a, b)\) by quadrature, which gives the MAP prior as a mixture of Beta distributions, and mapbern_post() integrates the two-dimensional posterior of \((\pi_c, \pi_d)\). Brock et al. (2023) use Stan for both steps and fit a mixture to the MCMC draws of the MAP prior. The likelihood is that of the exponential Bernoulli mixture model (expbern_post()) with hazards \(-\log(1 - \pi)\); only the priors differ.

Example 

prior <- map_beta(events = c(9, 11, 10), n = c(100, 100, 100))
attr(prior, "moments")
#>       mean         sd 
#> 0.10334757 0.03403532
nrow(prior)
#> [1] 1422
head(prior, 3)
#>            w   shape1   shape2
#> 1 0.04203266 17.25062 148.2004
#> 2 0.04030330 14.91639 128.1470
#> 3 0.03702683 15.25908 150.1920
set.seed(2)
n <- 200
drug <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.75)
y <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(drug == 1, 0.18, 0.095))
fit <- mapbern_post(y, t = rep(1, n), k = 3, prior_c = prior)
fit
#> Model: MAPBERN 
#> Tested quantity: ratio rr = pi_d / pi_c
#> P(rr > 1 | data) = 0.8602
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no
#> Posterior of rr: mean 1.84, median 1.627, 95% interval (0.6569, 4.263)
#> Posterior of pi_d: mean 0.166, median 0.1648, 95% interval (0.09953, 0.2396)

A prior derived with the RBesT package can be used as well: the rows w, a and b of a mixbeta object are the columns w, shape1 and shape2 of prior_c.

# mix: a mixbeta object of the RBesT package
prior_c <- data.frame(w = mix["w", ], shape1 = mix["a", ],
                      shape2 = mix["b", ])

Numerical integration and comparison with MCMC

Against independent Python computations (dense composite Gauss-Legendre rules split exactly at \(\pi_d = rr_0 \pi_c\) for mapbern_post(), and a dense grid over \((a, b)\) for map_beta()), the largest absolute difference of the 34 compared quantities is 1.2e-05. A JAGS model with the mixture prior and latent treatment assignments gives:

quantity MCMC bssd judgement
P(pi_d > pi_c | data) 0.9574 0.9570 PASS
posterior mean of pi_c 0.1011 0.1014 PASS
MCMC proportion below the bssd posterior median 0.5000 0.4976 PASS

Reproduction of Brock et al. (2023)

The simulation of Tables 1 and 3 (inst/reproduce/reproduce_Brock2023_simulation.R) has not been run for this installation.

References

Brock, K., Chen, C., Ho, S., Fuller, G., Woolfolk, J., McShea, C. and Penard, N. (2023). A Bayesian method for safety signal detection in ongoing blinded randomised controlled trials. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 22(2), 378–395. https://doi.org/10.1002/pst.2278
